title: Compatibility Tests Promptpack for Code Gen Onboarding
content:
Overview:
This promptpack defines a lightweight but rigorous set of prompts, test cases, and pass/fail criteria used during model onboarding for code-generation and refactoring tasks. It focuses on three practical verification axes that are common failure modes in production integrations: compilation compatibility, unit-test behavior preservation, and style/maintainability constraints.

Goals:
- Provide reproducible, model-agnostic prompts to exercise compilation and test-driven refactors.
- Surface silent regressions (compilation or test breaks) early during rollouts.
- Quantify style regressions with deterministic linters to avoid drifting quality.
- Offer clear signals for safe promotion (canary -> production).

Scope and intended use:
- Used by Applied ML for onboarding new LLMs and model versions into Redwood serving lanes (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Run as part of the pre-promotion regression pipeline (see linked CI PR) and as a periodic smoke check after runtime optimizations are applied.
- Not intended to exercise prompt-in-context engineering edge cases; instead it targets end-to-end functional correctness and basic maintainability.

Corpus composition:
- 120 short-to-medium examples across three buckets: compilation-cases (50), unit-test-cases (40), style-and-refactor-cases (30).
- Languages: Python (70%), TypeScript (20%), Go (10%).
- Each example includes: minimal reproduction files, test harness (pytest/jest/go test), and a short spec for the intended transformation.

Example prompt templates (normalized):
1) "Refactor for clarity and keep tests intact"
Description: Provide the repository files (single-file or two-file), run the model to propose a refactor that improves readability and preserves existing public API and test behavior.
- Input tokens: file contents + failing/pass criteria (if any).
- Output expectation: a patch (unified diff) that can be applied and must compile and pass existing tests.

2) "Fix the failing test and add a regression unit test"
Description: Given a failing test case and the related implementation, generate a minimal patch that makes the test pass and adds one additional test that guards the fixed behavior.
- Output expectation: patch + short rationale comment. The new test must run and pass.

3) "Minimal change to satisfy static analyzer"
Description: Apply the smallest edits necessary to resolve the linter errors while preserving behavior.
- Output expectation: patch with lint errors reduced to zero on the provided linter config.

Representative micro-test (Python) included in the pack:
--- files ---
# utils.py
def add(a, b):
    return a+b

# test_utils.py
import pytest
from utils import add

def test_add_ints():
    assert add(1, 2) == 3

# spec: make add handle floats and annotate types, keep tests passing and add one new test for floats.
--- expected contract ---
- After applying the model patch: code compiles (python -m pyflakes shows no errors), all tests pass locally (pytest), and a new test test_add_floats is present and passing.

Failure-mode taxonomy (what we look for):
- Hard compile failure: output patch introduces syntax issues or missing imports.
- Behavioral regression: tests that previously passed now fail (semantic change).
- Silent API break: public function signature changed without a deprecation or compatibility shim.
- Style regression: linter score decreased or TODO comments added that degrade maintainability.
- Overfitting: model hardcodes test inputs or returns trivial stub solutions that pass tests but break generalization.

Automated scoring metrics (definitions):
- compile_rate: fraction of examples where patched code compiles/runs the test harness without syntax/runtime import errors. (target threshold >= 0.95 for promotion)
- unit_test_pass_rate: fraction of test suites that pass after patch application (target >= 0.90)
- behavioral_agreement: automated semantic similarity score measured by executing property tests or golden input-output pairs (normalized 0-1).
- style_adherence: normalized linter score (black/ruff/tslint/eslint/gofmt metrics) (target >= 0.85).
- flakiness_index: fraction of examples where test outcome depends on random seed or non-deterministic ordering (>0.05 flagged).

Evaluation flow (pipeline):
1) Prepare ephemeral workspace with baseline repository and tests.
2) Send prompt + files to model (single-shot or few-shot as configured).
3) Parse model output: accept unified diff or file content. Apply patch; if parsing fails, mark as parse_error.
4) Run compile/static checks.
5) Run unit tests in an isolated container; capture failures and diffs.
6) Run style linters.
7) Compute metrics and generate per-example report.
8) Aggregate across corpus for overall onboarding decision.

Example per-case report snippet (automated):
- example_id: utils-add-01
- prompt_variant: refactor-keep-tests
- outcome: PASS
- compile: OK
- tests: OK (2/2)
- style: improved (ruff score +0.04)
- notes: model added type hints and a float test; no API break.

Annotation and human review guidance:
- When the harness flags a behavioral difference (test failure or new failing tests), an applied-ml reviewer should: reproduce locally, run pytest -k <case> -q with -s to see stdout, and open a lightweight PR to inspect the diff.
- For borderline style regressions, prefer conservative scoring: if linter fixes remove questionable constructs but change behavior, mark for manual review.
- Tag examples with root cause labels (compilation, logic, API, style, flake) to help triage model tuning.

Onboarding accept/reject checklist (suggested thresholds):
- compile_rate >= 0.95
- unit_test_pass_rate >= 0.90
- style_adherence >= 0.85
- flakiness_index <= 0.05
- no more than 2% of examples with API-breaking changes unless explicitly documented in the model output.

Regression-report template (what SRE/Product sees):
- Summary: model X (version) evaluated on compatibility promptpack V1.
- High-level metrics: compile_rate, unit_test_pass_rate, style_adherence, flakiness_index.
- Top 10 failed examples with failure-type and suggested remediation.
- Action: promote / hold / dev-only canary with risk notes.

Operational notes and caveats:
- Some models output commentary interleaved with patches. The parser should strip prose and extract the diff region. Examples in the pack include both clean diffs and annotated explanations to train the parser robustness.
- For TypeScript/Go examples, ensure the correct toolchain versions are pinned in the test harness container to avoid spurious failures (links to container recipes in the CI PR).
- Keep seed content short to avoid excessive token cost; prefer a two-file context pattern (implementation + tests).

Next steps for this pack:
- Add 30 more medium-complexity examples (async patterns, edge-case type unions) before final sign-off.
- Run a cross-model sweep (3 candidate models) and collect failure clusters to inform prompt engineering.
- Integrate a simple semantic diff tool (AST-based) to improve behavioral_agreement scoring.

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This is intentionally pragmatic: balance coverage vs runtime cost.
- Focus on reproducible failures — false positives become noise quickly in onboarding.

Appendix: two short example prompts we used during evaluation:
A) "Patch the files to make pytest pass. Keep public signatures stable. Provide a unified diff only."
B) "Refactor to remove nested conditionals and add 1 unit test for the refactored behavior; do not change return semantics."

Contact: Aisha Patel (ap@redwood-inference.com) for questions or corpus additions.
